methodology.description: A deliberately fundamentals-only score. No macro overlay, technical analysis, hedge-fund crowding, momentum or analyst price targets are used in the rating. Daily macro/theme and financing-risk observations are shown separately in the metric tiles and do not alter the score.

holdings.name: ExxonMobil

dailyOverlay.note: Integrated refining makes XOM better positioned than pure upstream if the shortage remains concentrated in refined products rather than crude.

metrics: Funding risk: Low · valuation risk: Moderate
holdings.strength: Cash generation and capital returns are the cleanest in the portfolio. Q2 2026 produced $23.6B of operating cash flow and $17.2B of free cash flow, while the share count continues to fall.
holdings.weakness: Still a commodity business. Current earnings are helped by elevated oil and refining conditions, so normalized-cycle returns matter more than a single strong quarter.
holdings.verdict: High-quality cash compounder for an integrated oil major. Valuation is not cheap on trailing earnings, but forward valuation, balance-sheet resilience and shareholder returns keep the fundamentals strong.

holdings.name: CTOS Digital Berhad

dailyOverlay.note: Credit-data demand is mostly insulated from AI capex, El Nino and energy shocks; softer consumer/credit growth is the main macro offset.

metrics: Funding risk: Low · valuation risk: Moderate
holdings.strength: The combination of recurring credit-data demand, high gross margins, low leverage and strong cash conversion is attractive. Q2 2026 revenue rose about 10% year on year and net profit rose about 7%.
holdings.weakness: Growth has moderated from earlier years, the current ratio is below 1, and the dividend payout is high. The business needs continued execution in regional expansion to reaccelerate growth.
holdings.verdict: A much better fundamental proposition around current valuation than it was at its old premium multiples. Quality and cash generation are doing more work than narrative.

holdings.name: IOI Properties Group Berhad
holdings.status: Asset value is strong; earnings quality needs checking

dailyOverlay.note: High leverage makes lower yields helpful but financing quality remains the key macro sensitivity. The next fundamental reset should follow FY2026 Q4 results.

metrics: Funding risk: High · valuation risk: Moderate
holdings.strength: The asset base is substantial and the Singapore investment-property portfolio is contributing more as occupancy improves. Core earnings improved materially through FY2026 and the stock still trades below stated book value.
holdings.weakness: Leverage is high and reported earnings are distorted by fair-value gains, consolidation effects and property-cycle timing. Trailing P/E therefore overstates how cheap the operating business is.
holdings.verdict: Fundamentally investable, but not as clean as the headline earnings multiple suggests. The next score should be rebuilt after FY2026 Q4 results rather than relying on fair-value-heavy trailing profit.

holdings.name: YTL Power International Berhad
holdings.status: Great assets; balance-sheet and valuation discipline matter

dailyOverlay.note: Power scarcity and time-to-power strengthen the asset thesis, but heavy capex and leverage make cash conversion the decisive test as AI financing scrutiny rises.

metrics: Funding risk: High · valuation risk: High
holdings.strength: Power generation, regulated UK water, telecommunications and a rapidly expanding data-centre platform give YTL Power unusually valuable infrastructure optionality. Q4 improved sharply quarter on quarter as Singapore power pricing and data-centre ramp-up helped.
holdings.weakness: Full-year profit fell materially from FY2025, capital expenditure is very heavy, free cash flow is negative and leverage is substantial. The current valuation already assumes a meaningful data-centre earnings ramp.
holdings.verdict: The asset quality is better than the current cash-flow profile. Fundamentally attractive only if the large capex programme converts into durable data-centre and utility earnings rather than remaining a perpetual funding requirement.

holdings.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
holdings.status: Elite franchise, weak current cash economics

dailyOverlay.note: The thesis remains driven by franchise execution and GTA VI rather than Power Stack macro. Consumer softness and discount rates matter at the margin.

metrics: Funding risk: Low-Moderate · valuation risk: High
holdings.strength: Rockstar, 2K and Zynga give Take-Two one of the strongest IP portfolios in gaming. Recurrent consumer spending supplies a large recurring base and GTA VI creates a credible step-change in scale.
holdings.weakness: Current GAAP profitability and cash flow are weak: Q1 FY2027 produced a net loss and operating cash outflow. The valuation therefore relies heavily on future GTA VI monetisation and post-launch execution.
holdings.verdict: Business quality is much stronger than the present financial statements. The holding earns a middling fundamental score until the expected GTA VI earnings step-up becomes visible in cash flow rather than forecasts.

holdings.name: Tesla
holdings.status: Balance sheet strong; valuation outruns current earnings

dailyOverlay.note: Power scarcity strengthens Megapack/storage while AI-financing and ROI scrutiny increases the evidence threshold for autonomy and humanoid optionality.

metrics: Funding risk: Low · valuation risk: Very High
holdings.strength: The balance sheet is exceptionally strong and the energy-storage business is scaling rapidly. Tesla still has strategic optionality in autonomy, software, robotics and energy that conventional automakers do not have.
holdings.weakness: The core auto business has low current margins relative to valuation, Q2 produced negative free cash flow as capex surged, and the market price capitalises a large amount of AI/autonomy success before it is visible in earnings.
holdings.verdict: Financially solvent and strategically interesting, but fundamentally expensive. On a pure fundamentals-only framework, valuation is the dominant drag and optionality does not receive full credit until it monetises.

holdings.name: Green Packet Berhad

dailyOverlay.note: Weak cash economics and dilution risk make this exactly the type of small-cap exposure penalised by tighter funding-quality discipline.

metrics: TTM net margin: about -3% to -9% depending period basis
Funding risk: High · valuation risk: Speculative
holdings.strength: The absolute market value is small and the company has recently carried net cash rather than heavy financial debt. That limits immediate balance-sheet pressure relative to many distressed microcaps.
holdings.weakness: The company remains loss-making with very thin gross margins, weak returns on equity, poor financial-quality scores and dilution risk from a proposed private placement. Revenue scale has not translated into durable shareholder earnings.
holdings.verdict: This is the weakest holding on fundamentals by a wide margin. Any investment case currently depends on turnaround/speculation rather than demonstrated earnings quality, cash returns or a defensible valuation framework.
